defects_found_and_fixed: R7R-TOOLCHAIN-PIN: the declared codex binary no longer existed after an in-place CLI upgrade; every lane dispatch failed BEFORE SPAWNING, stopping the SBL EXECUTE and VERIFY lanes. Pin re-derived from the installed binary; the registry's two expected values re-pinned in the same commit.

R7R-POOL-NOTE-STALE: all three lanes' selection_note still claimed minimax was rank 1, contradicting the same file's declared_by, change_log and ordered_pool[0]. The note is now generated from ordered_pool[0].
R7R-C6-NONCE-HARDCODED: the self-check's C6 pinned round 1's nonce, so no later successful round could satisfy it. It now reads the nonce from the receipt.
R7R-D1-FAILOPEN-SKIP: a failed build became a SkipTest on ANY nonzero exit, so a broken build could hide behind an absent backend. Found by the independent checker (R7 round 4).
R7R-D2-VACUOUS-ORACLE: the W1 regression test accepted either boolean result, so it asserted nothing. It now requires a real bool that agrees with `python -m build --version`.

R7R-D3-NONZERO-IS-NOT-A-KILL: the mutation probe treated any nonzero pytest exit as a caught mutation, so an infrastructure error could pose as a kill. The summary line is now parsed and a nonzero exit with no failed/errored test is a probe failure.

R7R-S1-GIT-ENV-INHERITED: the probe copied the whole environment and overrode only three git variables, so GIT_COMMON_DIR or GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY could still point into the protected repository. Every git-location variable is now stripped.
R7R-S2-SYMLINKS-KEPT: copytree(symlinks=True) kept symlinks, so a mutation writing to a linked file could follow it back into the protected tree. The copy is now symlinks=False.

R7R-B1-MISSING-INTERPRETER-RAISED: _has_build() called subprocess.run on a candidate interpreter without exception handling, so a path that does not exist aborted the whole resolution with a traceback instead of moving to the next candidate.

R7R-B2-SKIP-MARKER-MISMATCH: the D1 repair's skip markers did not match the wording the builder actually prints, so on a runner with no build backend an environment gap was reported as a product failure. This is what turned hosted CI red for five runs.

R7R-B3-BACKEND-RESOLVED-TOO-EARLY: build() resolved a backend interpreter inline, so a test that stubbed the build COMMAND still needed a real backend. build() now takes the interpreter as an argument and resolves it only when the caller did not supply one.
R7R-B4-GIT-ABSENT-RAISED: the write-through invariant test raised FileNotFoundError when git was not on PATH. It now skips, because a missing tool is an environment gap.
